test_inputs.description: manifest dict whose edges key aliases the manifest dict itself

test_inputs.outcome: str(e) renders as args-tuple repr, not .message -- FUZZ-SCSHA-002

findings.root_cause: bindings/sc-sha-python/src/lib.rs::parse_digest (lines 99-106) discards ShaError::code() and returns a bare &'static str; its caller parse_nodes (lines 133-134) then hardcodes the wrapper code as SC_SHA_INVALID_MANIFEST instead of forwarding the real error code the way calculate_hash_py/calculate_composition_hash_py do.
findings.recommended_fix: Return Result<TemplateSha256, sc_sha::ShaError> from parse_digest and call error(py, e.code(), e.to_string()) at the call site; add a regression test asserting code == SC_SHA_INVALID_DIGEST.

findings.minimal_repro:
try: sc_sha.calculate_hash({'utf8_file_bytes': 'nope'})
except sc_sha.ScShaError as e: str(e)
findings.expected: str(e) is a readable message (or documented otherwise)
findings.observed: str(e) == "('SC_SHA_INVALID_INPUT', 'utf8_file_bytes must be bytes; encode text as UTF-8 explicitly')"
findings.root_cause: ScShaError extends PyException and passes (code, message) straight into args without a custom __str__, so Python's default BaseException.__str__ renders the args tuple's repr.
findings.recommended_fix: Add #[pymethods] fn __str__(&self) -> String { self.message.clone() } to ScShaError.
